toc.title: Advantages, limits, model selection and business value

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. AI: artificial intelligence; ROI: return on investment

  • Name the advantages of generative AI
  • Identify its disadvantages: hallucinations, interpretability, inaccuracy and nondeterminism
  • List the factors for choosing a model
  • Pick business value metrics such as ROI, efficiency and conversion rate

2Advantages, limits, model selection and business value

Running case

Cedar and Salt Weighs Its Pilots

  • Leaders are excited about the review-summary tool and the booking assistant
  • The risk team asks: what can go wrong, and how will we know it works?
  • Engineers must choose a model, and finance wants proof of value
  • Your job: separate real strengths from real limits, and name the right measures

What Generative AI Does Well

  • Adaptability: one model handles many tasks, steered by prompts
  • Responsiveness: it answers in seconds, any time of day
  • Conversational ability: it understands natural language and replies in kind
  • Content generation: it drafts text, images, code and summaries
  • Together they speed up work and make AI easier to use for non-experts
Exam tip

Adaptable, responsive, conversational and able to generate content: the advantages to remember.

Hallucinations

  • A hallucination is an incorrect or misleading output from a foundation model
  • Causes include poor or limited training data, overfitting, a limited context window and ambiguous language
  • Effects: bad decisions, misinformation and security risks
  • Reduce them with Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), specific prompts, Guardrails and monitoring
  • Hallucinations cannot be fully removed
Exam tip

A confident, wrong answer is a hallucination; grounding with RAG helps most.

Other Limits: Nondeterminism, Interpretability and Inaccuracy

Limit What it means What helps
Nondeterminism The same prompt can give different answers, because the model samples the next token A lower temperature for steadier output
Interpretability It is hard to explain why the model gave an answer Citations, evaluations, human review
Inaccuracy Answers can be wrong, outdated or biased Grounding, testing and monitoring
  • Generative AI also needs care with private data and cost control
Exam tip

Different answers to the same prompt: nondeterminism. Hard to explain: interpretability.

Factors for Choosing a Model

Factor Ask
Model type and modality Text, image, audio or multi-modal?
Performance requirements Quality on our task
Capabilities Reasoning, languages, tool use, context length
Constraints and compliance Data residency, license and rules we must meet
Cost Price per token, plus the cost to run
Latency How fast must answers arrive?
Model complexity Bigger is not always better
Exam tip

Test candidate models on your own task; do not choose by size alone.

Quality, Cost and Speed Trade-Offs

  • A larger model is often more capable, but it usually costs more and answers more slowly
  • A smaller model is cheaper and faster, and may be good enough for a narrow task
  • Match the model to the task: summarizing reviews needs less than complex planning
  • Evaluate a few models on real examples from your business
  • Revisit the choice as new models appear
Exam tip

The best model is the cheapest and fastest one that meets the quality bar.

Business Value and Metrics

Metric What it tells you
Return on investment (ROI) Value gained compared with cost
Efficiency Time or effort saved per task
Conversion rate Share of visitors who complete a goal, such as booking
Average revenue per user (ARPU) Revenue divided by users
Customer lifetime value Total expected revenue from a customer over time
Accuracy How often answers are right
Cross-domain performance Quality across different tasks and topics
Exam tip

Match the metric to the goal: sales means conversion, payback means ROI, speed means efficiency.

Measuring Value Honestly Beyond the guide

  • Track cost and value together: cost per outcome is AI cost divided by a business value metric
  • Many things move revenue, so attributing it to AI is hard: use tests against a control group
  • Be careful with output counts, such as lines of code, which can be gamed
  • Include quality and customer feedback, not only speed
  • Review the numbers regularly, not once
Exam tip

One number is never enough; pair a value metric with a cost metric.

What the Exam Asks: Capabilities, Limits and Value

  • An advantage: adaptability, responsiveness, conversational ability or content generation
  • A limit: hallucination, nondeterminism, interpretability or inaccuracy
  • A fix: RAG and Guardrails for hallucinations, a lower temperature for steadiness
  • A model factor: type, performance, capability, compliance, cost, latency or complexity
  • A business metric: ROI, efficiency, conversion rate, ARPU or customer lifetime value
Exam tip

Name the situation first, then the limit, factor or metric.

Design Check: Cedar and Salt's Pilot Review

What the team sees Name and answer
The assistant invents a cancellation policy Hallucination: ground it with RAG and Guardrails
The same question gets two different replies Nondeterminism: lower the temperature
Nobody can say why it answered that way Interpretability limit: add citations and review
Chat must be fast and cheap A smaller model, tested on real chats
Leaders want proof it sells more trips Conversion rate
Finance wants payback ROI and cost per outcome
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

3Exam Q&A

3.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Which of the following is an advantage of generative AI for a business?

  • AIt guarantees that every answer is factually correct and never changes
  • BIt removes the need for any human review of its answers
  • CIt can converse in natural language and generate new content on request
  • DIt runs without any cost for compute, tokens or storage
Show the answer

Answer: C. Generative AI is adaptable, responsive and conversational, and it can generate text, images and code. It does not guarantee correctness, it still benefits from human review, and it has costs.

S2Cedar and Salt's assistant confidently quotes a cancellation policy that does not exist. What is this called, and what helps most?

  • AOverfitting, which is fixed by training the model for longer
  • BA hallucination, which is reduced by grounding answers with RAG
  • CUnderfitting, which is fixed by using fewer training examples
  • DLatency, which is fixed by using a larger instance type
Show the answer

Answer: B. An incorrect or invented output from a foundation model is a hallucination. Retrieval Augmented Generation grounds answers in real company documents, and Guardrails and monitoring help too.

S3Which TWO are limitations of generative AI solutions? (Select TWO.)

  • AOutputs can be nondeterministic for the same prompt
  • BEvery response is fully explainable step by step
  • CResponses can contain hallucinations
  • DThe model can never be used for summarization
  • EThe model always returns identical text to every user
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Hallucinations and nondeterminism are well-known limits, along with limited interpretability and inaccuracy. The other options are false statements about generative AI.

S4The booking chat must answer within about a second and the budget is tight. Which approach to choosing a model fits best?

  • AAlways choose the largest model, because size is the only measure of quality
  • BChoose the most expensive model, because price shows quality
  • CChoose a model at random and skip testing, because they are all the same
  • DTest smaller, faster models on real chats and pick one that meets the quality bar
Show the answer

Answer: D. Latency and cost are selection factors, and a smaller model may be good enough for a narrow task. Evaluating candidates on real examples shows which one meets the quality bar at the lowest cost.

S5Leaders want evidence that the new assistant leads more visitors to complete a booking. Which metric measures this directly?

  • AConversion rate, the share of visitors who complete a booking
  • BModel size, the number of parameters held inside the model itself
  • CContext window, the number of tokens that a single prompt can hold
  • DTemperature, the setting that controls how random the answers are
Show the answer

Answer: A. Conversion rate is the share of visitors who complete a desired action, such as a booking, so it shows sales impact. Model size, context window and temperature describe the model, not business results.

4Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Advantages adaptability, responsiveness, conversational ability and content generation
Limits hallucinations, nondeterminism, interpretability and inaccuracy
Fixes RAG, Guardrails, prompts, monitoring and human review
Model factors type, performance, capabilities, compliance, cost, latency and complexity
Value ROI, efficiency, conversion rate, ARPU and customer lifetime value, with cost per outcome
